newsitem.title: USA: US FERC okays Dakota Gasification settlement rates.
newsitem.headline: US FERC okays Dakota Gasification settlement rates.

text.p: The U.S. Federal Energy Regulatory Commission Wednesday approved rates for synthetic natural gas agreed to in a settlement reached by the Dakota Gasification Co, three interstate natural gas pipelines and the Energy Department.

The order reversed a FERC administrative law judge's initial decision from December 29, 1995, which said the parties entered the settlement imprudently, excluded ratepayers from the negotiation, and that the rates were excessive.
While voting unanimously to reverse that decision, the commissioners said by approving the settlement rates they were accepting the least distasteful option.
"I suppose we are saying that all the options are poor ones, so we take the least objectionable," commissioner William Massey said.
The long-running case stemmed from a $2 billion coal gasification demonstration project in Buelah, North Dakota, that was conceived after the 1973 oil crisis
The plant was taken over by the Energy Department in 1985 when its original owners defaulted on $1.5 billion in government-backed loans.
With deregulation of the gas industry, the plant's fuel was no longer competitive.
"A good energy policy in one era is not necessarily a good one in another. Energy policy has a relatively short shelf-life," Commissioner James Hoecker said.

The plant's synthetic natural gas is bought by Tennessee Gas Pipeline, a subsidiary of Tenneco Inc, Transcontinental Gas Pipe Line Corp, a subsidiary of Transco Gas Co, and ANR Pipeline Co, a subsidiary of American Natural Resources Company.
The pipelines provide gas to customers mainly in the Midwest and the Northeast.
The commission said approving the settlement rates entailed less risk to ratepayers than other options that likely would involve litigation.
The commission also said it did not have broad authority to grant refunds assumed by the administrative law judge and the ratepayers.
The settlement rates provide a "reasonable transition mechanism for bringing market forces to bear," Commissioner Vicky Bailey said.
